text:
Alex: Quick signal from staging after the AWQ/FP8 KV-dtype rollout — p99 latency for ~8-16 token completions jumped by ~40% during tail bursts. See profiling below.
Marta: ugh, saw that metric too. Was that the compact-packing change you merged last week? :grimacing:
Alex: yes — the new compact buffer packing + eager compaction pass meant to reduce KV footprint. On paper it saves ~12% memory, but we're hitting allocator fragmentation under our micro-batch mix.
Sahil: can you paste the perf traces? curious whether it's kernel selection fallback or pure allocation stalls.
Alex: pasted critical snippets from perf-trace and allocator logs: 
```
[perf] p99 latency 12.3ms -> 17.1ms (8-token chat)
[allocator] alloc(geo_cache) failed -> triggered fallback slab reflow
[allocator] free small blocks delayed by compaction pass; high scatter of free_chunk_sizes
[kernel] selected attention_kernel_fast -> fallback attention_kernel_generic (higher mem temp)
```
June: that fallback is the smoking gun. When compaction runs it briefly shuffles small free regions which screws the slab heuristic and forces larger kernel temps to allocate.
Orlando: does this correlate with KV dtype? AWQ uses smaller storage but we upcast to fp16 for runtime ops — that increases transient workspace. If packing reduces long-lived KV but increases short-lived transient allocations we can get fragmentation.
Alex: exactly. Profiling snippet from nvtx markers: 
```
# timeline slice (ms)
0.0 - 0.8  batching enqueue
0.8 - 3.5  compaction pass (async)
3.5 - 6.0  kernel selection + kernel launch
6.0 - 6.6  fallback kernel temp alloc spikes
```
Marta: is compaction synchronous with request path in our current rollout? I thought we made it async.
Alex: we made the compaction worker async but it still grabs per-GPU allocator locks for short windows. Under bursty small batches the timing aligns badly.
Sahil: repro steps? want to run a focused microbenchmark.
Alex: curl-based repro that hits the staging model with small chat payloads in parallel: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STAGING' \
    -H 'X-Model: awq-ggml-fp8' \
    -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":12}' &
done; wait
```
June: thanks. Initial ideas: 1) throttle compaction frequency (increase idle window), 2) make compaction use a non-blocking free path (deferred-free queue processed by background thread that avoids allocator locks), 3) bump slab superblock coalescing threshold so small scatter doesn't break kernel temps.
Orlando: also consider a temporary mitigation: disable compaction for AWQ models until we have a packing strategy that is compaction-safe. Might be the fastest rollback.
Sahil: another thought — adapt kernel selection to prefer kernels with smaller transient workspace when free heap fragmentation is high. We already track free_heap_ratio; tune kernel selector to weight transient_temp requirement.
Alex: good call. That decouples compaction from kernel fallback. We can add a penalty term in the kernel scorer: 
```python
score = base_perf - alpha * transient_workspace_bytes - beta * p99_alloc_latency
```
Marta: action items?
Alex: I'll open a short PR to (A) gate compact compaction behind rw feature flag per-model, (B) add deferred-free queue that drains without taking global alloc lock, and (C) tweak kernel scorer to prefer low-temp kernels when free_heap_ratio < 0.25.
Sahil: I'll run the microbench and validate p99 with and without compaction on a staging GPU farm.
June: I'll own rollout revert if needed and coordinate with infra to scale the compaction worker count.
Orlando: perf-bot posted a baseline snapshot (attached) — PerfBot: baseline_s3://perf-dumps/staging/1791023456/trace.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Alex: thanks everyone. If we can keep compaction disabled for AWQ until we validate deferred-free path, we should avoid customer impact. I'll update the release notes and add a regression test. :hudson:
